title: Telemetry fabric: cross-border mirroring gating and tenant-aware analytics federation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a tenant-aware telemetry fabric that enables selective cross-border mirroring for usage analytics while enforcing per-tenant residency, PII gating, and legal flags. This ticket scopes the orchestration layer and validation/gating rules that sit between ingestion and the analytics replication pipeline. The solution must: 1) allow tenants to opt into multi-region mirroring or enforce single-region residency; 2) apply schema-level sensitive-field detection and masking before any cross-region replication; 3) keep an auditable decision trail for why a batch was mirrored or blocked; 4) support runtime policy updates without pipeline restarts; 5) degrade gracefully (local-only writes, queueing, or safe-drop) under outage conditions to meet SLOs and compliance constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine supports per-tenant residency flags and legal tags
Pipeline applies field-level masking rules and can tag telemetry batches as 'blocked', 'masked', or 'ok'
Replication orchestrator can be toggled to replicate to a secondary region per-tenant with zero-downtime policy updates
Audit logs include decision reason, policy version, and dataset checksum for every mirrored batch
Failover behavior documented and tested: local-only retention + fanout retry queue for 72 hours
technical_notes: We will implement a lightweight policy engine (policy DSL) that evaluates tenant metadata, dataset schema, and runtime flags. Policies are stored in Config Store with versioned keys.
Masking will be implemented as a pluggable pipeline step using existing schema registry; detection rules reuse the PII classifier from the event-enrichment service.
Replication controller will use affinity-aware routing: primary write region -> optional mirror regions. Mirrors are treated as best-effort with explicit audit markers.
We prefer eventual consistency for mirrored analytics; strong consistency maintained in the tenant's primary region only.
Telemetry batches will carry a signed metadata envelope (policy-v, tenant-id, timestamp, checksum) to make cross-region validation deterministic.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Option A (chosen): Per-tenant mirroring with policy engine — more flexible for enterprise tenants and fine-grained compliance controls but increases orchestration complexity.
Option B: Static region-based routing by tenant org only — simpler but brittle for tenants with mixed legal requirements and harder to change at runtime.
Option C: Global anonymization before any replication — safest compliance posture but may remove signals needed for product analytics and observability.
implementation_steps: 1. Design policy DSL and storage schema (Confluence: /docs/console-analytics/policy-dsl)
2. Extend ingestion pipeline to attach tenant metadata and pass through policy evaluator
3. Integrate PII classifier and masking transformer as pipeline stage
4. Build replication controller that reads policy decisions and enqueues cross-region fanout
5. Add audit trail generation and retention hooks to Log Store
6. Create canary tests and chaos scenarios to validate failover behaviors
7. Roll out in two phases: internal telemetry only -> opt-in customers -> default enablement for enterprise customers with contracts
risks: Policy mismatch between pipeline versions may cause unexpected blocking — mitigated via versioned policies and backward-compatible evaluators
Masking may be incomplete for new schema fields — mitigated by integration tests and observability alerts for 'unclassified fields'
Cross-region bandwidth costs may spike with naive mirroring — mitigated with sampling and configurable mirrors per dataset
Operational complexity: edge cases for rollbacks and partial mirrors — mitigated by an audit-first rollout and staging environment tests
qa_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluator and masking steps
End-to-end tests that simulate tenant opt-in/opt-out and validate audit logs
Performance tests for replication throughput with masking enabled
Compliance tests: inject synthetic PII fields and verify they are masked before leaving primary region
metrics: % of telemetry batches mirrored vs blocked per tenant
masking effectiveness (number of PII fields detected and masked)
audit log completeness (ratio of mirrored batches with a valid decision envelope)
cost delta (egress + storage) attributable to mirroring
